Problem
- `hack doctor` can now detect and repair hidden-ref vs legacy-branch divergence for git-backed tickets.
- We still do not have a dedicated migration/repair command for normalizing older repos or repairing ticket id collisions after bad imports.

Why this matters
- The divergence in event-agent showed that users can end up with split history across `refs/hack/tickets` and `refs/heads/hack/tickets`.
- Doctor can auto-repair the common branch/ref divergence, but deeper normalization should be explicit and scriptable.

Follow-up scope
- Add a dedicated tickets repair/migrate command for hidden-ref/legacy-ref normalization.
- Detect ticket id shadowing/collisions and offer safe renumbering or remapping.
- Document the migration path and recovery workflow.
- Reuse the doctor health model so repair surfaces stay consistent.

- Exercise at least one environment where the bridge IP is reachable and one where localhost fallback is used
- Prevent regressions in `hack global install` and `hack doctor --fix`

## Notes
- Current targeted tests are unit-level and Linux-mocked command tests
- A real backend probe is the remaining confidence gap before broad rollout

payload.body:
Context
We need a durable product and implementation contract for three distinct remote usage patterns that are currently blurred together: managed standalone runtime, remote workspace offload, and explicit remote run/instance. Current project execution config only models local vs remote and makes remote feel like one saved project mode, which is not sufficient for event-agent-style runners or branch-scoped one-off remote actions.

Why
Without this taxonomy, CLI docs, Desktop IA, and controller behavior will keep conflating node registration, remote instances, and dispatched runs. That creates muddy UX around Topology, project defaults, branch instances, and Mutagen/devcontainer behavior.

Scope
- Define the three remote modes and the boundaries between node, instance, and run.
- Decide what remains a saved project default versus what becomes an explicit action.
- Define where each concept lives in CLI docs, project detail UI, and topology UI.
- Preserve backward compatibility for local, local_edit_remote_run, and remote_devcontainer while clarifying their semantics.

Acceptance criteria
- A written product/engineering contract exists in-repo and is referenced by implementation tickets.
- The contract explicitly distinguishes managed standalone runtime, remote workspace offload, and explicit remote run/instance.
- The contract defines node vs instance vs run terminology and expected CLI/Desktop surfaces.
- The contract states that project execution mode is a default behavior, not the only remote behavior expression.
- The contract covers branch-scoped remote instances and parallel remote actions.

Learned from event-agent
- event-agent uses hack as a managed standalone runtime on EC2; that is not the same thing as a local workspace offloading to a remote node for resource reasons.
- Controller visibility is useful but optional for managed standalone runtime operation.
payload.title: Define remote mode taxonomy and explicit remote actions UX

payload.body:
Context
event-agent's QA runner currently owns custom git reset/clean/index.lock recovery behavior in shell scripts. We want a first-class hack primitive that automation hosts can call safely and idempotently.

Why
Runner cleanup logic should not live in repo-specific glue when the behavior is generic to managed standalone runtimes and remote automation hosts.

Scope
- Add `hack workspace reset`.
- Support reset by base ref, untracked cleanup, explicit excludes, and index.lock recovery.
- Emit stable JSON so supervisors can reason about what happened.

Acceptance criteria
- `hack workspace reset --base <ref>` exists and works on a dirty workspace.
- The command safely clears stale `.git/index.lock` when present.
- The command resets tracked changes and cleans untracked files while preserving explicit excludes.
- `--json` returns removed/reset/preserved details in a stable shape.
- Non-recoverable git failures produce actionable errors and non-zero exit code.

Learned from event-agent
- The QA runner needs a runner-safe cleanup primitive, not ad hoc shell wrapped around git.
- Cleanup must be safe for unattended hosts and explicit about what was preserved.
payload.title: Add hack workspace reset for unattended runners

payload.body:
Context
event-agent currently needs same-host fallback execution plus clear differentiation between command failure, no diff, no commit, PR created, and PR failure. Today that logic is bespoke and ambiguous.

Why
Managed standalone runtimes need the same artifact/run/approval pipeline as remote dispatch without requiring node registration, and supervisors need machine-readable terminal states instead of parsing freeform stderr.

Scope
- Add `hack dispatch run --local`.
- Add typed terminal states for `--pr`: completed, pr_created, no_diff, no_commit, pr_failed.
- Add distinct exit codes for the non-error terminal states where appropriate.
- Persist the terminal state in run artifacts/JSON.

Acceptance criteria
- `hack dispatch run --local` executes using the same run records, logs, artifacts, and approval policy as remote dispatch.
- `--local` does not require node configuration or gateway availability.
- `--pr` outcomes are emitted as typed terminal states in JSON and persisted run artifacts.
- CLI exit codes distinguish no_diff, no_commit, and pr_failed.
- Existing remote dispatch behavior remains backward compatible.

Learned from event-agent
- The QA runner needs a generic same-host fallback path.
- PR automation needs explicit machine-readable terminal states to avoid brittle supervisor logic.
payload.title: Add hack dispatch run --local and typed PR terminal states

payload.body:
Context
We need a first-class AWS backend comparable to existing provider bootstrap flows, but scoped to existing EC2 instances reached via SSM. event-agent's QA runner is the reference deployment shape.

Why
The current AWS story lives in repo-owned scripts. We want a generic controller-side bootstrap flow that can discover/start an instance, wait for SSM readiness, run optional bootstrap, initialize the remote node, and register it with the controller.

Scope
- Add `hack node provider aws bootstrap`.
- Use built-in AWS SDK integration, not shelling out to `aws`.
- Support instance-id or tag lookup, start-if-stopped, SSM wait, optional bootstrap command, remote `hack node init --json`, registration, and reprobe.
- Preserve endpoint and source metadata for downstream parity flows.

Acceptance criteria
- AWS bootstrap works against both running and stopped EC2 instances.
- The command does not require the external AWS CLI.
- Remote bootstrap stdout/stderr is surfaced on failure.
- Successful bootstrap registers a node with endpoint and source metadata preserved.
- Output supports JSON for automation.

Learned from event-agent
- EC2 lifecycle and bootstrap over SSM is already a working shape.
- hack should own node/runtime bootstrap, while project-specific env hydration and infra provisioning remain repo-owned.
payload.title: Implement AWS EC2 + SSM bootstrap for remote nodes

payload.body:
Context
AWS remote nodes are not complete unless they are exposed in Hack Desktop and participate in the same parity flows as other source-backed remote nodes: Topology visibility, explicit bootstrap from the app, local_edit_remote_run, Mutagen sync, and optional devcontainer attach.

Why
A CLI-only AWS bootstrap path would leave the overall remote-node UX inconsistent and would not satisfy the event-agent/offload use cases the product needs to support.

Scope
- Add Settings > Extensions > AWS defaults and diagnostics in the macOS app.
- Add Topology affordances for AWS bootstrap.
- Ensure AWS-registered nodes carry endpoint + SSH source metadata needed for Mutagen and devcontainer flows.
- Validate AWS nodes with explicit remote actions and remote workspace offload parity.

Acceptance criteria
- Desktop can save AWS defaults and trigger bootstrap.
- Topology can launch AWS node setup and refresh the resulting node state.
- AWS nodes can participate in source-backed remote workspace flows, including Mutagen and devcontainer attach.
- Documentation and parity validation cover the AWS path end-to-end.

Learned from event-agent
- Remote runtime alone is not enough; controller visibility and attach/sync affordances matter.
- SSH source metadata is required for the same usability level as other remote workspace flows.
payload.title: Add AWS Desktop/Topology integration and source-backed parity flows

payload.body:
Context
Once the generic runner primitives exist, event-agent should stop owning bespoke node-registration, auth verification, workspace cleanup, and fallback dispatch logic. The repo should remain the reference managed-standalone-runtime deployment, but only for project-owned pieces.

Why
The platform work is not complete until the reference consumer actually adopts it and proves the abstractions are sufficient.

Scope
- Replace custom node registration logic with `hack node ensure`.
- Replace custom auth preflight logic with `hack node auth verify`.
- Replace custom cleanup logic with `hack workspace reset`.
- Replace direct fallback execution/PR parsing logic with `hack dispatch run --local` and typed PR terminal states.
- Keep project-owned ECS env hydration, service wiring, wake/start/stop orchestration, and `HACK_REMOTE_RUNNER` behavior.

Acceptance criteria
- event-agent runner bootstrap no longer owns custom node ensure/auth/workspace-reset logic.
- Supervisor logic branches on typed dispatch terminal states instead of parsing ambiguous output.
- The QA runner remains operational on EC2 after migration.
- Any gaps discovered during migration are reflected back into hack tickets rather than reintroduced as bespoke shell.

Learned from event-agent
- It is the best reference for managed standalone runtime mode.
- The right split is platform-owned runner primitives plus repo-owned environment/service orchestration.
payload.title: Migrate event-agent QA runner to new hack runner primitives
